one_sentence: Wavefunction collapse requires exactly three irreducible, non-commutative operators sharing a single Hilbert space, a structure formally identical to the Nicene Trinity.
executive_summary: This paper argues that the von Neumann measurement chain, which produces an infinite regress of observers under unitary quantum evolution, can be terminated by a minimum operator structure of exactly three irreducible, non-commutative operators sharing a single Hilbert space. The derivation shows that one operator fails due to self-reference, two operators fail due to infinite regress and thermodynamic constraints from Landauer's principle, and three operators succeed because the third, generated as the commutator of the first two, couples structure to actuality without regress. The resulting structure exhibits ten necessary properties that match the ten core doctrines of Nicene Trinitarian theology (325 AD), including unity of essence, irreducibility, distinction, relational definition via commutator (encoding the Filioque), perfect coherence of the structuring operator (sinlessness as thermodynamic requirement), perichoresis, completeness, and temporal transcendence. The paper concludes that this triadic pattern appears independently across 21 domains with probability less than 10^-21, suggesting convergent discovery rather than coincidence.
short_summary: This document is a formal paper deriving the minimum operator structure sufficient to terminate the von Neumann measurement chain. The core structural claim is that exactly three irreducible, non-commutative operators sharing a single Hilbert space are required, with the third generated as the commutator of the first two. Key evidence includes operator-algebraic derivation showing one- and two-operator failure modes, thermodynamic constraints from Landauer's principle, and a ten-axiom isomorphism with Nicene Trinitarian theology. This matters because it provides a mathematically rigorous foundation for consciousness-fundamental ontology and demonstrates cross-domain convergence across 21 independent fields.
